_about: Legend: Hansel and Gretel (Grimm KHM 15, Hesse, 1812). Jonny 27 Nov 23:32 Berlin picked H1 (gingerbread rule + 'if she smells ME?') + E1 (Gretel baits the baiter, 'I'm turning' with a full mouth). Niche-findings build: glowing house + red eyes frame 0, kid host = Hansel, one history line (L11), re-hooks L07/L11/L18/L22. Captions upper third, word by word. Speakers N narrator, G grandmother, K kid (Hansel), R Gretel, W witch. Grimm's four weeks in the cage compressed to one night.

G.style: an old woman in her eighties, warm but stern, low slightly raspy voice, slow and calm

K.style: a twelve-year-old boy from a film, natural child actor, clearly a boy, voice not broken yet, curious and cheeky, speaks clearly with crisp diction

R.style: a nine-year-old girl from a film, natural child actress, clearly a girl, bright high young voice, clever and brave, speaks clearly

W.style: a thin old witch, sugary sing-song sweetness over something hungry, creaky high voice, slow, nothing like a kind grandmother

say.L11: The Brothers Grimm, eighteen twelve. Their first version is darker than the one you know.

lines: If you smell gingerbread at night... turn around.
urgent low whisper, off screen, over the tiny glowing house and the red eyes opening in a sugar window; Sol 27 Nov: shortened ('in the forest' dropped, the picture shows the forest)
small, scared, sniffing, already close to the door
Nine o'clock. Their father left them by a fire, deep in the forest. And this time, he wasn't coming back.
Last night, white pebbles led them home. Tonight, Hansel only had bread.
And the birds were hungry too.
Midnight. Something sweet drifted through the trees.
The Brothers Grimm, 1812. Their first version is darker than the one you know.
intrigued storyteller, a secret; over the walk toward the house, no stop (Sol: don't delay the house)
Walls of bread. A roof of cake. Windows of clear sugar.
Nibble, nibble, little mouse... who is nibbling at my house?
sing-song, sugary, from inside the house, slow
Come in, my sweet ones. There are pancakes.
Witches have red eyes. They can't see far. But they smell you... like animals do.
He smelled her house. She smelled him first.
sweet voice gone, cold and hungry
Hansel held out a chicken bone. Her eyes couldn't tell the difference.
But a bone only works until she gets hungry.
Fat or thin, I eat him at dawn. Girl! Light the oven.
Crawl in. See if it's hot.
I don't know how... Show me?
She lured them with sweets. Gretel lured her with one sweet little question.
By sunrise, they were running home, pockets full of her pearls.
